purpose: Define the controlled process for proposing, validating, reviewing, merging, and recording governance documentation changes.
principles: Governance changes must be isolated from runtime changes.
Each governance change must have explicit scope and ownership.
Evidence must be reproducible and machine-readable where practical.
Existing canonical artifacts must not be silently rewritten.
Checksums and validation results must accompany closure artifacts.
Temporary branches and worktrees must be removed after merge.

change_classes.description: Fixes inaccurate documentation without changing governance intent or ownership.
Adds new governed components, evidence, ownership, exposure, or dependency records.
Changes governance requirements, approval rules, or canonical decision criteria.
Records completion, integrity validation, or final state for a governance sequence.

required_pull_request_controls: Changes limited to docs/99-governance unless explicitly approved.
No deleted files unless the deletion is documented and approved.
JSON artifacts must pass syntax validation.
The branch must contain only intended commits.
The pull request must be mergeable and target main.
The merge commit must be verified on origin/main.
Temporary local and remote resources must be cleaned up.

update_workflow.name: classify
update_workflow.requirement: Declare the change class and intended outcome.

update_workflow.name: isolate
update_workflow.requirement: Create a clean branch and independent worktree.

update_workflow.name: validate
update_workflow.requirement: Validate syntax, checksums, scope, and file operations.

update_workflow.name: review
update_workflow.requirement: Open a pull request with explicit validation results.

update_workflow.name: merge
update_workflow.requirement: Merge only when scope and repository state are clean.

update_workflow.name: verify
update_workflow.requirement: Verify the merge commit and artifacts on origin/main.

update_workflow.name: close
update_workflow.requirement: Delete temporary branches, worktrees, and files.

requirements: Define the expiry or review date.
Preserve the exception decision as a governance artifact.
